title: How the Folk Woodblock gets built
question: One more call: does an approved comp govern the build, or does the written contract?

options.label: Comp-led
options.lineage: the chosen decision comp plus two composition variations, one approved, then rebuilt to match
options.thesis: The picture is law: I generate two more first-viewport compositions beside the one you chose, you approve one, and the finish review audits the build against it.
materials: composited rendered assets where CSS cannot match
options.viewport: Whichever of the three comps you approve, reproduced near pixel-for-pixel at 1440 wide, then extended to every page in the same grammar.
options.risk: Boldest composition on the table and the most fix rounds; the illustrated house section will likely ship as a rendered asset rather than hand-drawn SVG, and motion (block-by-block print registration) is at risk until reproduction holds.

options.label: Code-led
options.lineage: no comp of this page; the direction contract carries the ambition
options.thesis: No further comps. The FIRST VIEWPORT block, a named signature interaction (the house prints one colour block at a time as you scroll, keyblock last), and the motion grammar are written into the contract and audited in behavior.
options.viewport: The chosen comp returns at the finish review as the critique reference, what the image dared that the build did not.
options.risk: The house illustration and cut lettering are drawn in SVG by hand, so they will be simpler than the comp; the upside is a fully live, animatable, responsive artifact with no bitmap dependency.
